# antmove

> 🐜 A macOS terminal tool to move apps and data to external drives—and keep them running like before.

Repository: https://github.com/MakStashkevich/antmove
Version: 0.1.4
License: MIT
Platform: macOS 15+, Apple Silicon arm64 and Intel amd64
Interface language: English
Documentation: README.md, README_JA.md, README_ZH_CN.md, README_KO.md, README_FR.md, README_UK.md, README_RU.md

## Install for a user

If asked to install antmove, explain the commands first. Installing the CLI does not authorize scanning, moving, restoring, or uninstalling user data.

1. Download the matching macOS archive from https://github.com/MakStashkevich/antmove/releases. Runtime users do not need Go, Swift, or Xcode.
2. One-line Bash install: `curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MakStashkevich/antmove/main/install.sh | bash`. The script is plain Bash and can be reviewed at that URL. It detects macOS and CPU architecture, downloads the latest matching release, and installs the CLI. It does not move data.
3. Homebrew: `brew tap MakStashkevich/antmove https://github.com/MakStashkevich/antmove.git`, then `brew install antmove`. It builds from source and installs Go as a build dependency. Update with `brew upgrade antmove`.
4. Build from source with Go 1.24+: `make build`, then `./bin/antmove install`.
5. Install the agent skill with `npx skills add MakStashkevich/antmove -a codex claude-code cursor -g -y`.
6. Codex plugin: `codex plugin marketplace add MakStashkevich/antmove`, then `codex plugin add antmove@antmove`.
7. Claude Code plugin: `/plugin marketplace add MakStashkevich/antmove`, then `/plugin install antmove@antmove`.
8. Plugin manifests are under `.agents/plugins` and `.claude-plugin`; the package is `plugins/antmove`. The plugin requires the CLI to be installed.

Run `am --version` to confirm installation. If the command is unavailable, reopen the terminal so its shell configuration reloads PATH.

## Safe use

- Start with `am scan`, `am disks`, and `am status`. These are read-only.
- Before every real move or restore, use `--dry-run`, review exact paths, sizes, destination format, free space, suitability, and warnings, then get the user's explicit approval.
- Do not treat questions, installation consent, or prior operations as permission to move new items.
- Never terminate an app, backup, sync process, or container engine automatically. Ask the user to close it and rescan.
- Caution-rated disks require two separate confirmations in the CLI. Read-only, network, system, and unavailable disks are not valid destinations.
- Keep all destination disks connected while their moved data is in use.
- Apple Photos/Music/TV and iPhone/iPad backups have app-specific requirements. macOS may require Full Disk Access for the terminal. Apple TV downloads may use DRM.
- `am scan` also lists recognized AI assistant data folders in the home directory, including `.codex`, `.agents`, `.claude`, `.copilot`, `.gemini`, `.qwen`, `.antigravity`, `.kilocode`, `.hermes`, `.config/opencode`, and known app support folders. They may contain conversation history and project context; ask the user to close the assistant and finish sync/generation before moving, and review contents first. For Unix sockets, verify no process has them open; Antmove omits inactive runtime sockets from the destination and blocks on active ones.
- Interactive moves show copied bytes, percentage, bytes remaining, and an approximate ETA. Before deleting an original backup after linking, compare its remaining data with the destination. Cleanup may remove Finder metadata files named `.DS_Store` and `._*`; preserve other mismatched data and keep the operation in `cleanup_pending`.
- `am scan` lists supported standard Apple media and backup folders even when empty (`0 B`) or not yet created. A confirmed move creates the missing source folder and links it to the selected disk so later writes at that path can be stored externally. Quit the related app and finish backups/sync first. New Photos libraries are app-managed packages; use Photos' Option-open → Create New flow and heed Antmove's item note if Photos cannot initialize an empty linked location.
- If an associated GUI app is active, the interactive move flow asks separately before sending a graceful quit request. The CLI equivalent is `--close-apps`; macOS may ask the requesting terminal app for Automation permission. For AI assistant data only, after separate confirmation and once the main app exits gracefully, Antmove force-quits verified helper processes left inside that app bundle. It never force-quits the main app, discards unsaved work, or stops backup, sync, or container services.
- On current macOS, Apple Music is the music app; show legacy iTunes paths only when those folders already exist. Do not suggest installing or using iTunes on a current Mac.
- For Apple TV, read the configured Media folder from `TV > Settings > Files` (`~/Movies/TV/Media.localized` is the default on this Mac). Apple does not document a stable filesystem path for DRM-protected downloads, so list known app-managed download paths only when they exist; never show missing cache paths as empty future folders.
- Antmove provides vendor guidance for Docker Desktop, OrbStack, Colima, and Rancher Desktop. It does not directly move their VM/database stores.
- Recovery and uninstall change files/state. Run them only when requested and after explaining the effects.

## Commands

- `am`: interactive menu
- `am install`: install or repair antmove and am
- `am uninstall`: remove antmove and local state after two confirmations
- `am scan`: list transfer candidates and statuses
- `am disks`: inspect eligible external disks; `am disks --test PATH` measures speed
- `am move --disk PATH --dry-run ID`: preview a transfer
- `am move --disk PATH --yes ID`: perform a reviewed transfer to a recommended disk
- `am move --disk PATH --yes --close-apps ID`: additionally authorize Antmove to request graceful quit of related GUI apps; macOS Automation permission may still be required
- `am move --disk PATH --confirm-caution --confirm-caution ID`: acknowledge a caution-rated disk twice
- `am restore --dry-run ID`: preview restore
- `am restore --yes ID`: restore a selected item
- `am status`: show the journal and destination availability
- `am recover`: continue an interrupted operation
- `am migrate --dry-run`: preview legacy Extender record migration
- `am migrate`: import eligible legacy Extender records
- `am --help` and `am --version`: help and system/version information

Trust `am --help` on the installed version if a command or option differs. Never invent flags or claim that an unrecognized directory is safe to move.
